day_shape: 48 items: heavy regime-channel Defence Industry Day cycle featuring Iran's acting defence minister meeting foreign military attachés and touring underground missile facilities, IDF strikes in Deir al-Balah and southern Syria, JPost reports Iran cleared Iraqi tankers through Hormuz; nothing from UK Parliament, State Department, OFAC or IAEA.

threads.label: Iran defence industry day messaging
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB carried coordinated coverage of Defence Industry Day, including acting defence minister General Ibn al-Reza meeting foreign military attachés in Tehran and Chief of Staff General Abdollahi's visit to an underground ballistic missile production facility. Ibn al-Reza was quoted claiming Iran had inflicted "strategic defeat" on the US and Israel through indigenous weapons production.

threads.label: IDF strikes in Gaza and southern Syria
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed Hamas Deir al-Balah battalion company commander Sharif al-Hasanat in a strike in central Gaza, with Palestinian media reporting one dead. The IDF also confirmed a strike in Beit Jinn, southern Syria, targeting an operative it said was in final stages of preparing attacks; Syrian media reported one injured.

threads.label: IRGC backs state broadcaster in internal row
threads.summary: IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi sent a commendation letter to the head of IRIB praising its wartime performance, which Iran International framed as backing the broadcaster against President Pezeshkian and Speaker Ghalibaf. IRIB carried parallel content on the broadcaster's role during the war and its head's appearances at a "transformation exhibition".

threads.label: Hormuz transit and Trump trade threats
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Iran had granted a number of Iraqi oil tankers permission to transit the Strait of Hormuz following repeated requests from Baghdad. Speaker Qalibaf, responding to Trump threats against states trading with Iran, posted in English that neighbouring countries had sent "multiple messages" seeking new regional security and economic arrangements.

threads.label: Iran domestic economy strains
threads.summary: Iran International reported the central bank governor denied hyperinflation while a leading Tehran economist said it had already arrived. IRIB carried a private-sector proposal to take over guaranteed wheat purchases, with the agricultural faction citing an 8-million-toman per-capita wheat subsidy, and the ministry rejecting transfer of the bread subsidy.

events.title: A Hamas commander involved in attempts to restore the terror group's tunnels in Gaza was killed in a strike in the Strip's center earlier today, the IDF announces. The strike in Deir al-Balah killed Sharif al-Hasanat, identified by the army as a company commander in the terror group's Deir al-Balah battalion. "Throughout the war, the terrorist was involved in leading efforts to restore the underground infrastructure of the Hamas terror organization," the military says. The IDF justifies the strike amid the ceasefire by saying that Hasanat recently had been attempting to advance attacks. "The terrorist posed an immediate threat to our forces and was eliminated," the military adds.

events.summary_en: Al-Zaydi's commitment to send the Popular Mobilisation Forces law to the Iraqi Parliament. The Prime Minister of Iraq has committed to sending the law on the Popular Mobilisation Forces to parliament for voting and ratification within the next two weeks. Rafiq al-Salahi, an Iraqi parliament representative, said that Ali Falah al-Zaydi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, has committed to sending the Popular Mobilisation Forces law to parliament for voting and ratification within a maximum of two weeks. Al-Salahi added that in last Thursday's meeting, a number of parliament representatives and the Prime Minister reviewed vital and sensitive files, foremost among them the file of fighting corruption and developing the service situation.
